business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition) with codified commercial and corporate statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) signed 2006, in force 2012
Colombia-European Union (Peru, Ecuador) Trade Agreement (in force 2013)
Andean Community Decision 578 (bolstering reciprocal investment promotion)
Colombia-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (modified by Decree 1736 of 2020 creating the Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero - UIAF); Resolution 285 of 2007 (UIAF obligation to receive and analyze suspicious transaction reports); Law 1121 of 2006 (anti-terrorist financing measures); Law 1621 of 2013 (intelligence regime); Decree 2555 of 2010 (financial system prudential rules as applicable); Law 2195 of 2022 (anti-corruption and beneficial ownership disclosure); Decree 1357 of 2021 (implementation of Law 2195); Circular Básica Jurídica of Superintendencia de Sociedades (external circular 100-000003 of 2018 requiring SAS entities engaged in high-risk fields but not software to register UBO declarations); Act 144 of 2019 of Superintendencia de Sociedades on Beneficial Owner registry; Law 222 of 1995 (corporate supervision and UBO duties); Decreto 1074 of 2015 (Sole Regulatory Decree for Commerce, sections on restructuring and registration); FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 as transposed by Colombia's AML/CFT National Strategy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence and Representation (Existence Certificate) of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chamber of Commerce and Registry of the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia acceded to the Apostille Convention on December 2010, effective May 16, 2011)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation formalities (Poder General o Especial)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the settlor/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in Colombia (Notaría) and submitted to Superintendencia de Sociedades portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal Colombian notarial protocol; foreign documents apostilled if remote

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each UBO and legal representative (data page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry authority or notary in origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Orden de Presentación / Paz y Salvo) for foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or competent tax authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Statement of Source of Funds / AML Compliance Declaration for Initial Capital Contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative and/​or shareholder notarized before Colombian Notary (Notaría)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal Colombian notarial act, no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, legal representatives, and officers against the following lists: (1) United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List; (2) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (3) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions; (4) Colombia's National Council for Sanctions and asset freezing list (Consejo Nacional Contra el Lavado de Activos, Decree 1736 of 2020); (5) INTERPOL Red Notices; (6) World Bank and IDB sanctioned entities; (7) Colombian Prosecutor General (Fiscalía) public corruption registries. PEP determination must include domestic Colombian politically exposed persons (senators, representatives, governors, mayors, ministers, judges, military commanders, central bank officials) and foreign PEPs (heads of state, ministers, senior judges). Enhanced due diligence is required when any UBO or counterparty is a PEP; the AML program (SAGRILAFT) must be implemented per Superintendencia de Sociedades External Circular 100-000005 of 2014 (updated by Circular 100-000011 of 2021). Non-compliance yields administrative fines up to COP 2.5 billion (approx. USD 620,000) per violation. Software development (ISIC 6201) is classified as low risk, but a formal SAGRILAFT document with risk matrices, transaction monitoring thresholds, and periodic UBO verification is mandatory for companies with gross assets exceeding 30,000 minimum monthly legal wages (approx. COP 39 billion) or gross revenue exceeding 30,000 SMMLV. If asset thresholds are below, a simplified risk matrix is still required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (portal https://www.rues.org.co) operating under the authority of the Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá for Bogotá domicile). Name reservation is electronically processed through the RUES Homonymy and Negative Certificate (Certificado de Homogeneidad y Denominación).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be composed of Spanish-language commercial denomination or a synthetic denomination in Roman alphabet; the S.A.S. type suffix 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' or the abbreviation 'S.A.S.' must be included. Entities may register a name in English provided it uses Latin script and is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered denomination. All official filings, bylaws, and registration documentation must be in Spanish; foreign-language documents require a Colombian certified translator (Traductor Oficial) and apostille. The doctrine prohibits names that differ only in accent marks, spacing, or terminal suffixes when compared to existing registrations. Names that include numeric sequences or geographic references are permissible but must avoid misleading attribution to governmental, public, or international institutions. Where a foreign parent name is imported (e.g., a global brand), the same exact spelling must be declared, and a trademark clearance with SIC (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio) is recommended.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon electronic submission via RUES, the chamber of commerce issues a preliminary availability certificate; if rejection occurs, grounds may include homonymy with an existing registered name or a trademark infringement notice. Prohibited token use or recognition of public institution affiliation yields rejection with an administrative motivation. An administrative appeal (recurso de reposición) must be filed with the same chamber of commerce within ten (10) business days of notification pursuant to Article 76 of Law 1437 of 2011 (Código de Procedimiento Administrativo). If dismissed, the applicant may file an appeal in the hierarchical superior (Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio) within five (5) business days. In parallel, a revised alternative name may be immediately reselected through RUES without requiring the exhaustion of the appeal. Rectification of a denomination after registration requires a notarized corporate resolution documenting the amendment and a new RUES filing, triggering re-payment of registration tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for incorporation and general correspondence; Colombia recognizes virtual or address service offices for S.A.S. purposes if the registered address serves for law-mandated notifications, judicial service (notificaciones judiciales), and UIAF/Superintendencia formal notices. However, for ISIC 6201 software and cloud operations, the tax authority (DIAN) may disallow a pure virtual address for VAT invoicing registration and permanent establishment risk avoidance if actual management is performed abroad. Given vertical ERP/CRM cloud operations with Colombian data processing, the company must demonstrate at least one physical management office, a permanent employee or a rent contract, plus local telecom infrastructure to sustain the 'effective place of management' doctrine under Article 12-1 of Law 1819 of 2016 (anti-tax-haven rules). Virtual office alone is not sufficient for banking onboarding with local Colombian banks (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda), which typically require a physical inspection of commercial premises by their risk department before opening corporate account.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_to_Moderate (risk assessed at 15-20% annually). The Superintendencia de Sociedades conducts administrative visitation under Article 83 of Law 222 of 1995 on a sampling basis; for low-risk technology firms with no public funds, no licenses, and low-value real estate, on-site inspections are uncommon. However, once the company registers with DIAN for VAT and exercises the CREE labor and tax credits, DIAN has the authority to perform unannounced visits to verify billing equipment (facturación electrónica) and payroll records under Article 617 of the Tax Code. Additionally, if the company accumulates cross-border remittance transactions exceeding USD 10,000, UIAF's transaction reporting threshold triggers, heightening the odds of an audit visit. Probability increases to 40% if foreign directors are listed without Colombian contact personnel.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and homonymy certificate (Certificado de Homogeneidad) via RUES
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local chamber of commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Decreto 1074 of 2015 and chamber fee schedule; small administrative fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Constitución por Documento Privado ante Notario o Acta de Asamblea)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff per Decreto 960 of 1970 and Código de Notariado; market fee for a standard one-appointment incorporation deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) at the Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff scaled to registered capital; baseline for no/minimum capital is approximately COP 150,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing (Beneficiario Final) with Superintendencia de Sociedades
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No filing fee; compliance obligation under Act 144 of 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization for foreign corporate documents (passport, power of attorney, certificate of existence, good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authority (e.g., US Secretary of State, UK FCDO, UAE Ministry of Justice) and/or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public tariff per apostille authority, typically USD 5-20 per document; consular legalization fees range USD 100-300; assumes 5 documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified sworn translator (Traductor Oficial) registered with Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of COP 8,000-15,000 per 180-character line; typical bundle of 8-10 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting, and filing coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Colombian law firm or corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rates in Bogotá/Medellín; fixed fee for standard S.A.S. incorporation package with UBO mapping and AML SAGRILAFT skeleton

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registro Único Tributario (RUT) and NIT pre-registration with DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free online through DIAN portal; requires chamber of commerce certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAGRILAFT simplified risk matrix preparation by compliance officer or external consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent compliance consultant or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk technology entities, including draft documentation for UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening policy

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic signature and certified mail costs for notarial appointments (if using remote powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Actual disbursements; electronic signature platforms in Colombia charge approximately COP 50,000 per validation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 on the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada, Articles 1-50, in harmony with the Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio) Articles 98-120 on commercial companies and Articles 352-353 on corporate registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered office, operating through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) digital platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución y Estatutos Sociales (Private Incorporation Deed and Bylaws), subsequently registered in the Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an S.A.S. The shareholders freely determine paid-up and subscribed capital. If subscribed capital is stated, at least 20% of the subscribed shares must be paid up at execution. No escrow or bank account is mandated for the paid-in amount unless the bylaws voluntarily require one for management of contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY] S.A.S. (Excerpt). The undersigned sole shareholder, constituting the company, resolves: (1) the subscription and payment of 100% of the share capital, represented by issued shares, with the equivalent consideration received and recorded in the treasury; (2) the establishment of the registered office at [address], and to adopt the required legal address for all corporate notifications; (3) the appointment of the President and Secretary; (4) the granting of powers to the General Manager to execute contractual and banking formalities; and (5) the approval of the corporate incorporation document as executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name at the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) / Cámara de Comercio electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a certificate of availability (Certificado de Homónimos) through VUE, selecting the S.A.S. type and the proposed company name. Provide the shareholder's identification data and requested municipal address. The certificate is valid for 30 calendar days. Pay the online nominal fee and download the certificate to attach to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and identification document of the requesting shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name conflict is returned, the applicant will receive a list of available similar denominations and must revise the name request to avoid identity with existing registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Private Incorporation Deed and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders, directly through VUE authenticated signature; intervention of a notary is optional
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución y Estatutos Sociales in Spanish, indicating the shareholders' identities, share subscription, capital payment plan, and the bylaws. The document must be digitally signed by all shareholders using VUE authentication. No notarial deed is mandatory for an S.A.S., but notarization is permitted if shareholders prefer.
required_dossiers: Valid civil identification (cédula) or passport for each shareholder
RUT pre-registration of the company, when available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed contains defects, the VUE system returns a precise correction report. The shareholders file a corrective version and re-submit; once registered, a new RUT upgrading process must be completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Commercial Registry (Matrícula Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with commercial registry powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation deed in the VUE portal for commercial registration. Upon approval, the Chamber of Commerce issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, a certified extract containing the corporate name, NIT, and legal representation. The company receives its registration number and Matrícula Mercantil.
required_dossiers: Executed private incorporation deed (PDF via VUE)
Identification documents of shareholders and legal representatives
Proof of payment of registration fees or decimal assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber of Commerce queries the filing, the applicant must upload an adjusted deed or supplementary evidence through VUE within 10 business days. The registry is also subject to administrative review by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RUT and Activate Tax and Social Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, the RUT is automatically updated or created online. For digital invoicing, request the technical key for electronic invoicing and, if applicable, the digital signature certificate. Open tax files for national and municipal taxes (VAT, income tax, ICA). Verify availability of sectoral incentives for software and IT services.
required_dossiers: Articles of association and proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN determines a mismatch in the RUT address or economic activity classification, submit a rectified RUT and supporting lease or deed, and request the DIAN service center to activate the responsible economic activity and tax regime.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Physical Facilities and Complete Municipal Business Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the commercial use of the physical office with the municipal government. Submit the compatible use or installation right (Derecho de Instalación) application. The software office is not subject to an industrial authorization. The municipality verifies compliance with urban and police provisions for non-manufacturing offices.
required_dossiers: Certificate of building safety or technical statement for occupancy
Identification of the legal representative and payment of the municipal fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal application is rejected or queried, submit the corrected technical statement or lease annexes to the local business authority and resubmit the request within 15 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is applicable for software and cloud services under ISIC 6201; the activity is service-based and only local municipal authorization is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Information Technology Service – Non-Manufacturing Office Activity (commercial registration and municipal occupancy permit; no sector-specific license).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible) / Regional Autonomous Corporation (CAR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for cloud software activities; no EIA study is required under Law 99 of 1993 and applicable environmental planning regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Non-industrial discharges are limited to office sanitary wastewater, which must comply with municipal sewerage parameters under Decree 1076 of 2015 and local RAS standards. No VOC or point-source emission standards apply. Electronic waste generated by office equipment must be delivered to licensed WEEE operators under Resolution 761 of 2010.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for commercial offices under the National Firefighter Corps (Cuerpo de Bomberos), structural load clearance of the leased premises, and occupational health and safety clearance for the physical workplace are required before staff operates in the office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (National Tax and Customs Directorate); official portal www.dian.gov.co; electronic taxpayer portal Sede Electrónica (MUISCA/ Nueva DIAN) for registrations, filings, e-invoicing and refund proceedings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute and apostille a corporate power of attorney appointing a Colombian resident legal representative and tax agent. Step 2: Formalize the S.A.S. deed before a Notary and register it with the local Cámara de Comercio, obtaining the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal. Step 3: File the electronic Pre-RUT through the DIAN Sede Electrónica using the representative's digital signature. Step 4: Receive the statutory NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and definitive RUT (Registro Único Tributario), which assigns the taxpayer as responsible for IVA (VAT) under the Régimen Común, income tax at entity level, withholding agency, and electronic invoicing. Step 5: Activate the Firma Electrónica and the CUFE/CUDS stamping credentials and contract an authorized proveedor tecnológico for facturación electrónica. Step 6: Register the ISIC 6201 activity and, if goods are exported, obtain the export registration in the customs and exchange systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Colombian S.A.S. is a resident juridical person taxed on worldwide income (Articles 12 and 22 E.T. and Law 2277/2022), with a headline corporate income tax rate of 35% for 2024; Pass_Through_Eligible: No, no fiscal transparency to shareholders; Territorial_Scope: Worldwide for a Colombian-resident S.A.S.; Tax_Exempt_Zone: N/A unless the entity obtains a DIAN-recognized Zona Franca user status, which is elective, not default.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombian tax law does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include: (i) the SIMPLE regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación, Ley 2010/2019, Article 905 E.T.), elective for S.A.S. with gross revenues up to 100,000 UVT in the prior year, replacing income tax with a combined progressive rate of approximately 1.8% to 14.5%; (ii) application for Zona Franca status with reduced 15% income tax for qualifying software exporters; (iii) optional selection of the bimonthly VAT filing and refund period based on export volume; (iv) election to keep exchange-rate accounting gains under specific rules; and (v) no hybrid mismatch deductions are available to a Colombian resident S.A.S., and BEPS Action 2 limitations are applied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Value Added Tax), governed by Articles 420-489 E.T., Law 1819/2016, Decreto 1625/2016; no federal or regional GST overlap; one national VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis turnover registration threshold for corporate entities: VAT registration in the RUT is mandatory from the first taxable act or service provision by a S.A.S. (Articles 437 and 555-2 E.T.). The only relevant threshold is the SIMPLE regime eligibility ceiling of 100,000 UVT (~COP 4,706,500,000 for 2024), which does not waive VAT registration obligations for export-oriented software suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta, FEV) under Resolución DIAN 000165/2023 and the unified Anexo Técnico: the S.A.S. or its authorized proveedor tecnológico must transmit XML invoices to DIAN web-services before issuance, incorporate the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) or CUDS digital stamping, exchange acceptance/rejection events with the buyer, and report export invoices under the 'Exportación de servicios' modality; export invoices cite the DEX or the service export contract and zero-rate VAT. Refund claims and the VAT return (Form 300) are cross-validated against the electronic invoice database.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Article 481 E.T., Decree 1073/2017 and Decreto 1625/2016 to exported goods and to exported services, including vertical ERP/CRM and SaaS software (ISIC 6201), when all conditions are met: (i) the service is covered by the statutory list comprising software development, maintenance, technical support, licenses and cloud services; (ii) the acquirer is a foreign resident without a Colombian permanent establishment and the service produces no economic use or benefit inside Colombia; (iii) the contract, FEV, technical reports and cloud usage logs evidence service delivery and foreign consumption; (iv) payment is received in foreign currency through the Colombian foreign exchange market; (v) the exporter files the Declaración de Cambio and, for supporting inputs, maintains full VAT credits, which become refundable as saldos a favor.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DEX (Declaración de Exportación) for goods or, for services, the service-export contract and technical certificate of execution abroad
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill for goods; for software services, the electronic delivery log and cloud consumption report
Factura Comercial (Commercial Invoice) and FEV - Factura Electrónica de Venta de Exportación with CUFE stamp and explicit 0% VAT clause
Declaración de Cambio (FX declaration, Form 1 / DC-1) and Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Colombian authorized intermediary
Foreign client corporate identification and a written statement confirming the non-existence of a Colombian permanent establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN reconciles the FEV/CUFE e-invoice database, the VAT return Form 300, the DEX customs statements and the Banco de la República foreign-exchange database to verify that export proceeds entered Colombia within the 180-day period. If the zero-rating claim fails, DIAN may: (i) reassess the 19% IVA on the disputed export invoices with default interest under Article 635 E.T. and inflation adjustment; (ii) impose the imprecision penalty of 100% to 200% of the omitted VAT under Article 643 E.T.; (iii) levy electronic-invoicing fines of up to 1% of gross revenue under Article 652 E.T.; (iv) deny or retroactively claw back the VAT refund balance (saldos a favor) and disallow the corresponding input credits; and (v) refer the case for criminal tax fraud under Article 402 of the Colombian Criminal Code if forged export invoices or exchange declarations are detected; ordinary audits may extend beyond three years in cases of omitted declarations, with longer limitation periods in criminal and penalty proceedings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, acting through its Exchange Operations Department and the regulations of the Comisión de Cambios; prudential supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed floating exchange rate with full convertibility on current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, royalties, and profit remittances, subject to mandatory channeling through authorized exchange market intermediaries for receipts and payments with non-residents. Capital account operations, including foreign direct investment and cross-border loans, remain generally free but require ex post registration with the Banco de la República and must be channeled through local banks. Dividend and profit remittances to foreign shareholders are lawful, provided the S.A.S. is tax-compliant, the payment is supported by certified financial statements, and the funds are routed via a Colombian bank through the exchange market using the appropriate CAMALEIS declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from the sale of software and technology services, when classified as goods or services under Colombian export rules, must be channeled through an authorized local financial intermediary within the statutory term of six months from the date of shipment or service completion, unless an extension is expressly approved by the Banco de la República. The mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts is 100% of the invoiced foreign currency amount, meaning the funds must be brought into Colombia and converted into Colombian pesos, or held in a foreign currency deposit account at a local authorized bank that reports the position to the central bank. Early repatriation is permitted, and documentary evidence of invoicing, invoice number, and customs or service export declaration must be submitted to the intermediary to complete the foreign exchange declaration.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore electronic money institutions and non-resident EMIs. Colombian law does not recognize foreign EMIs as authorized exchange intermediaries; only institutions supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia may open local accounts, receive FX channeled funds, or access the interbank clearing infrastructure. Offshore EMIs can be used only as auxiliary billing or client-payment software interfaces, provided they are not used for custody of COP funds or for settlement of export proceeds without a local partner bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the legal representative and beneficial owners is generally mandatory for the initial onboarding of a foreign-owned S.A.S. at tier-one banks. Remote onboarding may be available where the bank has adopted biometric and electronic verification tools authorized by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia, but the practical rule is that at least one Colombian director or an appointed legal representative with power of attorney will be interviewed in person before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpectedly complex ownership chain involving foreign trusts or holding companies in low-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group corporate chart, notarized certificates of incumbency, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent, a transparency declaration identifying all direct and indirect beneficial owners with greater than 10% interest, and a written explanation of the economic purpose of the Colombian S.A.S.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution arriving from a third-party jurisdiction unrelated to the shareholder's residence or the entity's declared business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreements, bank statements of the remitting shareholder evidencing lawful source of funds, underlying board minutes approving the contribution, a certified copy of the public deed or S.A.S. documentation, and the completed foreign direct investment registration form submitted to the Banco de la República.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared vertical cloud software activities and expected payment flows from unrelated CRM customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts with international clients, proof of actual service delivery, invoice registers, detailed descriptions of the ERP and CRM modules, and a treasury policy showing expected settlement cycles, accounts receivable aging, and client onboarding procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch in corporate address, tax ID, or legal representative data against the national chamber of commerce records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date certificate from the Cámara de Comercio, valid Colombian tax identification number (NIT) certification, notarized and apostilled appointment of the directors, and signed representation agreement in favor of the local banking representative if the foreign director is unavailable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment for the Colombian S.A.S. must be registered with the Banco de la República using the foreign investment registration form and the associated CAMALEIS line, and the capital injection must be wired as a clean international transfer via SWIFT MT103 to an operational or escrow account held by an authorized Colombian bank. The wire must include the investor's legal name, the company's NIT, the purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment in software and technology services, and a reference to the notarized share subscription agreement. The receiving bank will require a copy of the registration confirmation before crediting the funds to the company's account; failure to register within the statutory timeline may trigger exchange regime penalties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for vendor payments, licensing royalties, and subcontractor disbursements shall be executed through SWIFT MT103 instructions from the Colombian operating account or, when transaction volume and risk justify it, through irrevocable documentary commercial letters of credit issued by a Colombian bank. For service and software subscription payments, clean payment transfers under the foreign exchange intermediary must be accompanied by the relevant import declaration or service contract, pro-forma invoice, and exchange declaration to satisfy the Banco de la República's periodic reporting duties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery-based forward contracts between COP and USD entered into with a Colombian authorized bank or broker, covering a specific trade invoice or committed capital flow.

Non-deliverable forwards entered into with offshore counterparties, provided the settlement difference is paid outside Colombia and the contract is not settled in COP within the national territory; such instruments are used for board-approved hedging of foreign-exchange risk.
Cross-currency swaps between COP and USD executed through a local authorized intermediary, limited to matching cash-flow positions in the ERP subscription and capital expenditure cycle.
Exchange-traded or OTC options on USD/COP for income protection and for the management of contingent balance-sheet risk arising from non-collection of foreign receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Commercial Registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil) in the RUES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce with territorial jurisdiction (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January through 31 March following the business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge on the registration tariff; the company cannot obtain a valid registration certificate or effect subsequent registrations until renewed, and persistent non-renewal exposes the company to eventual cancellation of the commercial registration by the Chamber.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax and Complementary Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the DIAN-fixed filing window for legal persons covering the preceding calendar year; exact days are announced by DIAN Resolution and are allocated by the last two NIT digits, typically in March-April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay by the deadline triggers late-filing fines under ET Arts. 641 and 642, default interest, inability to obtain tax clearance certificates, and, after official assessment, enforced collection by DIAN.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation or Update (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the confirmation period established by DIAN Resolution for the calendar year; the S.A.S. must ratify or update its ultimate beneficial owner data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccuracy, delay, or omission is subject to DIAN fines for flawed or unsupplied information under ET Art. 651 and may impair the company's active tax status and transactional certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Municipal Industry and Commerce Return (Impuesto de Industria y Comercio - ICA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Treasury or District Finance Department of the place where software services are rendered (e.g., Bogotá D.C. - Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually according to the applicable municipal calendar, generally between January and April for the previous taxable period; exact dates are set by the subnational treasury resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and payment accrue penalties and interest under the territorial tax code; continued non-filing may lead to official default assessment and enforced collection by the municipality.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory Revisor Fiscal is mandatory for an S.A.S. if at the close of the preceding year total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV or gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV; below those thresholds an independent audit is not statutorily imposed, but can be required by bylaws, shareholder agreement, or group parent policies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS framework incorporated through Law 1314 of 2009 and Decree 2420 of 2015 (DUR 2420/2015); S.A.S. entities classified as Group 2 apply IFRS for SMEs, while smaller or listed/public-interest entities apply Group 3 micro-entity standards or full IFRS as applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each S.A.S. must maintain an accurate internal record of all natural persons who, directly or indirectly, own or control at least 10% of the company or exercise significant management influence. This information must be confirmed annually in the DIAN Beneficiario Final system; share transfers occurring during the year must be incorporated into an extraordinary update when required by the rules, but do not replace the ordinary annual confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes Book of Shareholders' Meetings (Acta de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Minutes Book of Board of Directors (Acta de Junta Directiva, if board appointed)
Annual Financial Statements and Approval Minutes retained at the registered office
UBO / final beneficiary documentation file maintained at the legal seat

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 250 - 800 per year for a registered office, local representation and compliance assistance in Colombia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500 - 4,500 per engagement for a small-to-mid-size S.A.S. that becomes subject to Revisor Fiscal/independent audit
